key_insight: Prompt-conditioned LLMs are limited by information and alignment constraints, so some task families remain indistinguishable or unattainable even with infinite data or scaling.
engineering_relevance: For system designers, this means better prompts alone cannot guarantee correctness; richer interfaces such as multimodal inputs or external memory may be needed to recover task information.
method: Models user–system interaction as a bilevel cheap-talk game.
Separates task inference from task execution.
Derives PAC-Bayes-style bounds to separate estimation error from irreducible limits.
evidence_signal: The paper is a theoretical analysis in the abstract, relying on formal bounds and capacity arguments rather than experimental evaluation data.
watch_item: The conclusions depend on assumptions about channel capacity and alignment constraints, so practical impact will vary with the interface and safety policy design.
paper_title: On the Limits of Prompt-Conditioned Language Models as General-Purpose Learners
